text: Which genes enriched or enhanced in cervix or vagina are enhanced in suprabasal keratinocytes (single-cell), have no detectable mRNA in liver, and are not secreted into the blood?
plan: Tissue category (RNA): Cervix, Vagina / Tissue enriched, Group enriched, Tissue enhanced AND Cell type category (scRNA): Suprabasal keratinocytes / Cell type enhanced AND Tissue category (RNA): Liver / Not detected AND NOT Secretome annotation: Secreted to blood
understanding: Identify genes that have tissue RNA specificity enriched or enhanced in cervix or vagina, are enhanced in suprabasal keratinocytes based on single-cell RNA-seq specificity categories, have no detectable RNA expression in liver, and are not classified as secreted to blood in the secretome annotation.

trail.requirement: enriched or enhanced in cervix or vagina
trail.why: Filters for genes categorized as tissue enriched, group enriched, or tissue enhanced in either the cervix or vagina.

The requirement specifically asks for genes enhanced in suprabasal keratinocytes at the single-cell level, matching the 'Suprabasal keratinocytes' cell type with the 'Cell type enhanced' specificity category.
Selecting 'liver' at level 1 and 'Not detected' at level 2 filters for genes with mRNA below the detection cut-off of 1 nTPM in liver.
The requirement excludes genes secreted into the blood, which directly corresponds to the 'Secreted to blood' category under Secretome annotation.

requirements.requirement: enriched or enhanced in cervix or vagina
requirements.why: Tissue category (RNA) classifies tissue specificity categories across consensus RNA-seq datasets, allowing selection of cervix and vagina with enriched/enhanced categories.
Cell type category (scRNA) measures RNA specificity across single cell types, including suprabasal keratinocytes.
Tissue category (RNA) represents consensus tissue mRNA specificity and distribution, supporting categories for genes not detected in specific tissues like liver.
Secretome annotation classifies predicted secreted proteins by destination, including 'Secreted to blood', which is excluded using NOT.
